en.name: Bernadette Soubirous
en.summary: Poor French peasant girl to whom the Virgin Mary appeared eighteen times at Lourdes in 1858.
en.body: Bernadette was a sickly fourteen-year-old from an impoverished miller's family in Lourdes, France, when she reported the first of eighteen apparitions of a young lady in white at the grotto of Massabielle in February 1858. The lady, who Bernadette said identified herself as "the Immaculate Conception," instructed her to dig for a spring, drink from it, and tell the local clergy to build a chapel there. Despite fierce local skepticism and interrogation by civil and religious authorities, Bernadette never wavered in her account. She later joined the Sisters of Charity of Nevers, living a hidden life of illness and humility until her death in 1858. The shrine that grew from her testimony became one of the world's most visited Catholic pilgrimage sites.
